Which transports to enable, and what they cost, is `ditto-mesh-networking`'s topic,
otherwise <https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/sync/customizing-transport-configurations>.
This file is the Rust API.

## CAP-06 Customizing transports

Edit the live configuration in place. The block is generated from a test that CI runs
(it asserts the change took effect):

<!-- snippet: rust-transport-config -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
fn configure_transports(ditto: &Ditto) {
    // Start from the live config; TransportConfig::default() is NOT TransportConfig::new().
    ditto.update_transport_config(|config| {
        config.peer_to_peer.bluetooth_le.enabled = false;
        config.peer_to_peer.lan.enabled = true;
        config.listen.tcp.enabled = true;
        config.listen.tcp.interface_ip = "0.0.0.0".to_string();
        config.listen.tcp.port = 4040;
        config
            .connect
            .tcp_servers
            .insert("10.0.0.5:4040".to_string());
    });
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

| Call | Notes |
|---|---|
| `ditto.update_transport_config(\|config\| { … })` | start from the current config: the safe default |
| `ditto.transport_config() -> TransportConfig` | a copy |
| `ditto.set_transport_config(config)` | replaces everything; **panics** if Ditto rejects the config |
| `TransportConfig::new()` | every transport off, sensible ports and intervals |
| `config.enable_all_peer_to_peer()` | BLE, LAN, AWDL, Wi-Fi Aware (not multicast) |

## The config tree

`TransportConfig` (`dittolive_ditto::transport`, all `Clone + Default + PartialEq +
Serialize + Deserialize`):

| Path | Type | `new()` value |
|---|---|---|
| `peer_to_peer.bluetooth_le.enabled` | `bool` | `false` |
| `peer_to_peer.lan.{enabled, mdns_enabled, multicast_enabled}` | `bool` | `false`, `true`, `true` |
| `peer_to_peer.awdl.enabled`, `peer_to_peer.wifi_aware.enabled` | `bool` | `false` (Apple / Android radios; not on Linux) |
| `peer_to_peer.multicast_beta` | `MulticastBetaConfig` | off; 5.1.0+, private beta ([preview.md](preview.md)) |
| `connect.tcp_servers` | `HashSet<String>` (`"host:port"`) | empty |
| `connect.websocket_urls` | `HashSet<String>` (`"wss://…"`) | empty; filled from the URL in Server mode |
| `connect.retry_interval` | `Duration` | 5 s |
| `listen.tcp.{enabled, interface_ip, port}` | `bool`, `String`, `u16` | `false`, `"[::]"`, `4040` |
| `listen.http.{enabled, interface_ip, port, websocket_sync, tls_key_path, tls_certificate_path}` | | `false`, `"[::]"`, `80`, `true`, … |
| `global.sync_group`, `global.routing_hint` | `u32` | `0` |

The instance's starting config is not `new()`: Ditto enables the platform's stable
peer-to-peer transports. Read it with `transport_config()` before deciding what to turn
off.

## Rules

- **Never start from `TransportConfig::default()`.** It is derived and differs from
  `new()`: LAN mDNS and multicast discovery off, `retry_interval` 0, empty
  `interface_ip`, port 0 (executed). The same applies to a partially specified config
  deserialized with serde (`#[serde(default)]` fills from `Default`).
- Servers and gateways on fixed hosts usually want `listen.tcp` on a fixed port plus
  `connect.tcp_servers` on the clients, rather than relying on mDNS across subnets or
  container networks.
- `listen.http` with `websocket_sync` lets WebSocket clients sync to this peer; put TLS
  in front of it or set the TLS paths.
- `global.sync_group` partitions peers that share a database ID; `routing_hint` is set
  only on Ditto's advice (<https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/deployment/setting-routing-hints>).
- Changing transports restarts them; avoid doing it on a hot path.
- Transport-condition observation (other SDKs' `observeTransportConditions`) is not
  exposed in the Rust SDK 5.2.0 public API.
